text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Green party wants to reformulate proposed reform of State regional administration with emphasis on efficiency, democracy.
- "Negative thinking day" turned into a positive event.
- Young Finnish architects' "forest atelier" awarded at Venice architecture biennale.
ETELA-SAIMAA
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says a linkage of the markka to the ERM would allow no manipulation of exchange rates.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Despite optimistic economic outlook, service-sector firms investing cautiously -- mainly in information technology. After rising by one fifth last year, investment growth likely to flatten out somewhat this year.
- Pension insurance money moving into government bonds and and stocks, while funds' lending to companies has declined.
- Neste's oil trading losses this year could exceed earlier estimate of 285 million markka, Neste CFO Veli-Matti Ropponen said. High crude oil prices to blame.
- Several Finnish listed companies have lowered their profit forecasts for this year.
- European Parliament hopes for 65 percent turnout in Finland's October Europarliament vote.
DEMARI
- Social Democrat parliamentary group leaders say the government's budget will be passed despite criticism of taxation measures.
AAMULEHTI
- Competition will keep price increase of new cars in check next year, one car dealer says. Prices of used cars may even fall.
- Prime Minister Lipponen urges uniformity in regional cross-border cooperation with Russia, saying current practice disjointed as regions try separately to achieve their goals.
TURUN SANOMAT
- State ombudsman for data privacy calls for more discussion on the use and registration of personal data, such as social security numbers.
- About 85 percent of Finnish women with breast implants are satisfied, study shows.
--Helsinki Newsroom +358-0-560 60 235
